SLIDE 01 OF 08 ACT I · THE PROBLEM

Learning "The Last 50 Feet" on the Water Carries High Financial Expense, Real Injury Risk, and Almost Zero Practice Reps.

Modern 30-to-52-foot cruisers like a Pursuit S 358, MJM 38, or 52' Twin-Inboard Yacht weigh 15,000–48,500 lb, have no brakes, and berth inside slips with 12 to 16 inches of clearance per side. Yet unlike aviation, racing, or golf, boaters have no safe practice cage—they are forced to learn live in front of the whole marina.

Reference Vessel #1: 2023 Pursuit S 358 (18,800 lb Loaded)

1. High Repair Expense & Lost Summer Weeks Financial Risk

In close quarters on Lake St. Clair or a crowded transient harbor, one gust or wrong lever crushes fiberglass against a piling, damages twin lower units, or scrapes a neighbor's yacht—triggering deductibles and stealing weeks out of a short 4-month Great Lakes summer waiting in a repair yard.

2. Real Personal Injury Risk to Family & Crew Safety Hazard

When an approach goes sideways, stressed spouses and guests instinctively reach out an arm or leg to fend off an 8-to-24-ton moving hull, jump prematurely onto wet finger piers, or catch hands in dock-line pinch points. You cannot safely rehearse high-wind recovery when mistakes endanger your crew.

3. Starved of Repetitions & Frozen Out 6 Months/Yr 1 Rep Per Outing

Skill requires repetition—yet a boat owner gets one high-stress docking attempt at the end of a Saturday with spectators watching, followed by six months (October–April) of zero helm time while the boat sits shrink-wrapped. Docking anxiety quietly caps enjoyment, spouse confidence, and boat upgrades.

Sourced Industry Context: 2024 USCG Boating Statistics report 3,887 incidents and ~$88M in property damage (collision was the first event in 56% of incidents; low-speed marina scrapes under $2,000 go uncounted). 2024 Michigan DNR data ranks operator inexperience among top contributing factors.
The Solution — A Physical-Helm + Display-Agnostic Visual Bay (Walk-In Surround Pod or 360° VR): Put real boat controls in the operator's hands while surrounding them with 1:1 slip clearances, wind shear, and marina hazards safely indoors.
Compact 8 ft × 8 ft Controlled Helm Environment: Real physical wheel, dual binnacle throttles, integrated bow thruster toggle, and 3-axis joystick—paired with 360° stereoscopic depth perception over the bow and stern.
How MoorPrepared Solves Close-Quarters Training
  • Physical Where Hands Touch: Real steering wheel, dual binnacles, bow thruster toggle, and 3-axis joystick build transferable muscle memory.
  • Eyes-Up 360° Depth Perception: Stereoscopic VR lets skippers look naturally over the bow, beam, and transom to judge pilings to the inch.
  • 20+ Reps in 45 Minutes: Hit a 2-second Reset button after any gusty mistake—pushing limits safely with zero repair or injury risk.
  • Year-Round On-Demand Practice: Train October through April with a Licensed Captain, Digital Coach, or Solo before launch day.

SLIDE 05 OF 08 ACT II · WHY SERIOUS BOATERS & CAPTAINS TRUST IT (CORE IP)

In a 14-Foot Slip with 16 Inches of Clearance, Vessel-Specific Physics Is What Makes It Real.

Generic boat games drive every hull like an arcade car. Customers and dealer captains trust MoorPrepared because our shared illustrative 3-DOF physics engine models each hull's specific windage, momentum, keel drag, prop walk, and bow thruster limits—with physical piling bounce when inches run out.

Shared Illustrative 3-DOF Physics · Pre-Sea-Trial Values

Proof 01: Same Captain Inputs, Opposite Slip Outcome

Both vessels start properly lined up at x = 0 ft 0 in just outside the 14 ft 0 in finger slip. The captain applies the exact coordinated crab inputs calibrated for Boat A (Pursuit S 358, sea-slate blue)—bringing it straight down the centerline with 1 ft 3 in of clearance on both sides (SAFE). Given those exact same inputs, Boat B (52' Twin-Inboard Cabin Cruiser, warm brass) catches more lateral windage and physically bounces off the leeward piling.

Compare Any Two Vessels (Shared Engine) Same starting line & helm timeline
Vessel ParameterBoat A (Pursuit)Boat B (52')

High-Wind Amplification & Marina Wind-Shadow Traps Fwind ∝ Vwind2

In 18 knots of crosswind, lateral wind force is 36× higher than in a 3-knot breeze—and backing out of a windy fairway into the sheltered lee of a 52' neighbor yacht drops wind on the stern while the bow is still pushed sideways. Because holding the line takes ~3× higher baseline power (and can saturate a joystick's 1,800 RPM cap around 20 kt), a 2-second hesitation rapidly drains stopping & AGM thruster margin.

SLIDE 06 OF 08 ACT II · INSTANT FEEDBACK & REAL SEAMANSHIP

Objective Bird's-Eye Replay Turns Every Run Into an "Aha" Moment—and Celebrates the Safe Go-Around.

Just as golfers love seeing club-path data on a launch monitor, boaters love seeing their exact hull trace from above right after a maneuver—or hitting our 15-second Instant Rewind ("Mulligan with Physics") to re-fly an 18-knot gust until they recognize an unstable approach early (Run A) instead of forcing a recovery (Run B).

50Hz Rewind Ring-Buffer · Behavioral Realism

1. Celebrating the Bail-Out + 15s Physics Rewind Run A vs Run B

When an approach is blown off-center by an 18-knot gust outside the pilings, amateur instinct is to jam throttle and hold the S 358's 3.0 HP (2.2 kW) bow thruster until AGM/thermal protection cuts it out (Run B). With our 15-second ring-buffer rewind, trainees rewind right to t = 3.6 s and practice aborting cleanly (Run A).

2. Captain-Verified Behavioral Realism 8-Test Suite

Rather than treating physics as an academic science project, our 50 Hz behavioral engine is tuned to the exact shift delays, rotational time constants, pivot-point shifts, and wind-shadow traps that build transferable muscle memory—verified against an 8-maneuver Captain acceptance suite and on-water S 358 trials.

3. Display-Agnostic UX: Walk-In Surround Pod vs. 360° VR Customer-First Decision

Because our engine is display-agnostic, we are evaluating a 3–4 Person Walk-In 270°–360° Multi-Screen Surround Pod (zero headset friction, zero nausea, progressive-lens friendly, using per-boat virtual camera framing to simulate hull distances) head-to-head against 360° VR—letting customer experience and sightline realism drive the final choice.

Interactive After-Action Replay: Scrub the timeline or jump to key decision moments to compare Run A (Controlled Go-Around — Good Seamanship) against Run B (Forced High-Power Entry — Piling Bounce).
t = 14.0 s / 20.0 s
RUN A (SEA-SAGE) — CONTROLLED BAIL-OUT & GO-AROUND

SLIDE 07 OF 08 ACT III · MARKET FIT & BUILDING THE GO-TO-MARKET

A Proven Indoor-Bay Category Applied to Boating's Biggest Gap—Embedded Where Boaters Buy and Gather.

We aren't inventing the simulator category: aviation, motorsports, and Northern indoor golf already proved customers flock to dedicated bays when a high-stakes, weather-bound skill moves indoors. Partnering with premier dealerships and yacht clubs puts MoorPrepared directly into an existing customer flywheel.

Anchor GTM Lens: Jefferson Beach Yacht Sales

1. Proven Category, Wide-Open Marine Vertical Market Fit

Flight schools, racing sim centers, and winter TrackMan golf clubs thrive because customers want safe reps out of the weather. Recreational boating has higher close-quarters anxiety and a 6-month Great Lakes winter layoff—yet zero scaled simulator leader today.

2. Showroom Bays & Mobile Trailer Pods Zero Cold CAC

Rather than opening retail storefronts from scratch, a compact 3–4 person walk-in bay (~8 ft × 8 ft) drops inside flagship showrooms (like JBYS) or into a portable enclosed trailer ("Mobile Bridge Pod") that rolls directly up to yacht clubs (GPYC), spring launch clinics, and boat shows.

3. One Physical Pod Morphs Across Every Boat Brand Fleet Leverage

Because the four core helm controls are universal while per-boat software camera framing and virtual hull rendering dynamically adjust sightlines, eye height, and propulsion topology, a single pod switches from a 25' Single I/O to a 35' Pursuit S 358 to a 52' Twin-Inboard Yacht in seconds—across either Multi-Screen Surround or VR.
